lead.headline: US CBDC Ban Becomes Law as Circle Secures Banking License, Marking Divergent Regulatory Paths for Public and Private Digital Dollars
lead.tldr: The US has effectively foreclosed on a Fed-issued digital dollar while accelerating private stablecoin integration into traditional banking, creating a lopsided policy architecture that privileges commercial issuers over sovereign monetary innovation.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the US is betting its digital currency future on private actors rather than public infrastructure.

top_signals.title: Housing bill that includes a CBDC ban passed into law without Trump's signature
top_signals.summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act has officially become law, incorporating a critical provision that prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). The bill passed into law without requiring a signature from President Trump.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The CBDC ban becoming law without Trump's signature signals durable bipartisan opposition to sovereign digital currency in the US, removing a strategic option that 130+ central banks are actively exploring and ceding first-mover advantage in programmable monetary infrastructure to other jurisdictions.

top_signals.title: Circle wins licence for some US banking activities
top_signals.summary: Circle has been granted a license to operate as a trust bank, allowing it to engage in specific US banking activities. This regulatory approval is seen as a significant step for the stablecoin issuer's integration with traditional financial systems.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Circle's trust bank license represents the most consequential regulatory normalization of stablecoin issuers to date, effectively creating a template for how dollar-backed tokens absorb banking functions without triggering full bank charter requirements—a structural win for incumbents that raises barriers for new entrants.

top_signals.title: Stablecoins May Improve FX Access but Worsen Currency Runs: IMF
top_signals.summary: The IMF has released a paper analyzing the impact of dollar-backed stablecoins on foreign exchange markets. While they may improve FX access, the IMF warns they could accelerate currency runs by signaling dollar scarcity to the market.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The IMF's warning on stablecoin-driven currency runs introduces a credible macroprudential risk narrative that could justify capital controls or issuance restrictions in emerging markets, directly threatening the TAM expansion thesis that underpins much stablecoin valuation.

top_signals.title: Robinhood to Launch AI Agent Feature For Crypto Trading
top_signals.summary: Robinhood is expanding its AI agent trading capabilities to include cryptocurrency. This feature will allow agentic accounts to execute crypto trades on behalf of users, mirroring its existing functionality for equities and options.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Robinhood's AI agent expansion into crypto validates agentic execution as a genuine product category rather than vaporware, but the real signal is mainstream brokerage infrastructure treating automated crypto trading as a retention tool comparable to equities—a normalization milestone with compliance implications.

top_signals.title: Kraken Plans AI-Powered Trading App Overhaul, CNBC Reports
top_signals.summary: Kraken is planning a comprehensive overhaul of its trading application to integrate AI-powered trading agents. This move reflects a broader trend of crypto exchanges and fintech firms adopting artificial intelligence to enhance digital finance services.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Kraken's AI-powered app overhaul confirms that exchange differentiation is shifting from asset breadth and fee structures to execution intelligence, a capex-intensive pivot that favors scaled players and may accelerate consolidation among mid-tier venues unable to fund AI development.

deals.summary: Empery Digital has sold 1,400 bitcoins to facilitate a strategic pivot toward artificial intelligence and to settle outstanding debts. A portion of the proceeds was used to acquire a 25% stake in an AI data center campus project.

on_the_radar.title: Senate Democrats call for hearings into Trump’s ties to crypto amid CLARITY Act discussions16m, Senate Democrats call for hearings into Trump’s ties to crypto amid CLARITY Act discussionsFive senators called for committee hearings to investigate US President Donald Trump’s policies potentially being influenced by crypto funding from United Arab Emirates-linked and other entities.
on_the_radar.summary: Five US Senators are calling for committee hearings to investigate whether President Donald Trump's policies are being influenced by crypto funding. The inquiry specifically focuses on ties to UAE-linked entities and coincides with discussions regarding the CLARITY Act.

on_the_radar.title: SK Hynix’s $26.5 billion US listing brought to Telegram users via xStocks
on_the_radar.summary: Tokenized shares of SK Hynix are now available to users on the Solana blockchain via platforms like Backpack, xStocks, and Ondo Finance. This integration allows Telegram users to access these assets through the xStocks interface.

on_the_radar.title: New Hampshire Council Votes Down $100M Bitcoin Bonds
on_the_radar.summary: The New Hampshire executive council rejected a proposal to issue $100 million in Bitcoin-backed bonds. The vote ended 3-2 against the Business Finance Authority's plan.

on_the_radar.title: Backpack joins race for 24/7 stock markets with tokenized equities21m
on_the_radar.summary: Backpack is entering the tokenized equities market to enable 24/7 trading of stocks. This move aims to merge traditional finance assets with the accessibility and efficiency of blockchain technology.

on_the_radar.title: Kraken to relaunch its mobile app with agentic trading and advise at the center
on_the_radar.summary: Kraken is relaunching its mobile application with a focus on agentic trading. The update will introduce autonomous AI agents capable of monitoring markets, suggesting trades, and executing them for users.

on_the_radar.title: Federal Reserve Taps A16z Co-Founder for Monetary Policy Task Force
on_the_radar.summary: The Federal Reserve has appointed a16z co-founder Marc Andreessen to lead a task force focused on the economic impact of emerging technologies. The initiative specifically aims to analyze how advancements like AI influence monetary policy.

on_the_radar.title: Oracle Exploit Drains $9M From Bonzo Lend on Hedera
on_the_radar.summary: Bonzo Lend suffered a loss of approximately $9 million due to a price manipulation attack. The exploit targeted the SAUCE token by leveraging a flaw in Supra's oracle verifier on the Hedera network.

on_the_radar.title: DOJ moves to dismiss charges against alleged $722M BitClub fraudster: Report29m, DOJ moves to dismiss charges against alleged $722M BitClub fraudster: ReportMatthew Goettsche was set to face trial in October for conspiracy to commit wire fraud and selling unregistered securities.
on_the_radar.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice is reportedly moving to dismiss charges against Matthew Goettsche, who was accused of involvement in a $722 million fraud scheme related to BitClub. Goettsche had been facing charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and selling unregistered securities.

linkedin_post: A lot of people saw the CBDC ban and filed it under 'crypto wins against the state.' That is the wrong read. The 21st Century ROAD Act becoming law without Trump's signature kills a Fed-issued digital dollar. Simultaneously, Circle secures a trust bank license for specific US banking activities. These are not separate stories. They are the same story: the US is choosing a private stablecoin architecture over a public one, and doing so with unusual speed. The market is pricing this as deregulation, but we have underwritten stablecoin policy risk on sovereign competition and it feels mispriced. The IMF's paper today flags exactly what we worry about—dollar-backed stablecoins improving FX access while accelerating currency runs in stressed economies. That is not a bug in the design; it is the design, and it creates political blowback risk that 'pro-crypto' legislation does not address. The value proposition is shifting from 'digital dollar for everyone' to 'digital dollar for everyone except when their central bank needs control.' I'd watch how emerging market regulators respond to Circle's banking integration versus how they treated unlicensed issuers. The repricing risk is not in Washington. It is in Lagos, Jakarta, and Buenos Aires. Whether stablecoin access gets ring-fenced by capital controls before it gets scaled by banking partnerships—that is the testable thing. Equities got the headline; the FX desk got the risk.
